title: Finite Tor amplitude descends from a finite principal localization cover
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $K^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules (modules $K^n$ and $R$-linear maps $d^n:K^n\to K^{n+1}$ with $d^{n+1}d^n=0$) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $a\le b$ be integers. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in R$, with $r\ge0$, generate the unit ideal, and write $R_{f_i}=R[1/f_i]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Use the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], specialized to the site with one object, only its identity morphism, and only the maximal covering sieve, so that sheaves of rings and modules are rings and modules. Derived tensor with an arbitrary module, placed in degree zero, is the ordinary-module derived tensor product computed on K-flat models by [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model]. If, for every $i$, the localized complex $K^\bullet\otimes_R R_{f_i}$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ (meaning that $H^n((K^\bullet\otimes_R R_{f_i})\otimes_{R_{f_i}}^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $R_{f_i}$-module $N$ and every $n\notin[a,b]$), then $K^\bullet$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$: $H^n(K^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for every $R$-module $M$ and every $n\notin[a,b]$.
